rows.grounds: present active verb expressing the act of bewildering or deluding
compound object denoting the foremost immortals together with their adversaries
name of the goddess Lakṣmī, subject of the deluding action
particle marking the stated understanding or conclusion
compound indicating those by whom the manifestations or play of the Self are known

items.question: By what recognition is Indirā's delusion of gods and their foes understood as the Self's manifestation?
premises: Indirā actively deludes both the foremost immortals and their enemies.
This deluding power is apprehended in a specific way.
Those who have known the Self's manifestations recognize this delusion as such.
items.inference: The bewilderment caused by Indirā is not mere confusion but is recognized as a manifestation of the Self by those who know its play.
uncertainties: The exact compound analysis of amara+varya+tat+ripūn as a coordinate or hierarchical grouping is context-dependent.
vidita+ātma+vibhramaiḥ may denote agents characterized by this knowledge or the means of recognition.
items.plain_english: Indirā deludes the best of the immortals and their enemies; thus it is understood by those who have known the manifestations of the Self.
